executiveChairman.name: Jean Bilong
authority: paid promotion and token grant approval

agentCannot: hold private keys or seed phrases
move BTC, SOL, SATA, or LP tokens
make legal, tax, or investment commitments
promise price, redemption, or market support

items.title: Enable approved-only X social agent posting
items.summary: Allow the X social agent to publish only queue items that the Executive Chairman has already approved.
items.rationale: This gives SATA an operating-company social cadence without allowing agents to invent market claims or approve posts themselves.
items.proposedAction: Set GitHub repo variable SATA_X_AGENT_ENABLE_POSTING=true, add X_ACCESS_TOKEN as a GitHub Actions secret, change social queue mode to approved-only-automation, and approve individual posts before publication.
riskReview: Agent cannot publish unless the specific queue item is marked approved.
Posts still pass social policy validation before publishing.
Paid or token-compensated posts remain separate approval items.
items.publicDisclosure: Automated posts must remain factual and source-linked. Paid or token-compensated content requires explicit Sponsored/Paid Partnership disclosure.

items.title: Adopt standard promoter intake policy
items.summary: Require promoter proposals to include deliverables, compensation, draft copy, disclosure policy, and anti-bot confirmation before any payment or token grant.
items.rationale: SATA can work with legitimate promoters only if compensation is disclosed and claims stay factual.
items.proposedAction: Use the promoter intake checklist for every promoter and pay only after the approved deliverable is live and unchanged.
riskReview: Reject fake engagement, pump language, investor targeting, guaranteed results, and undisclosed paid promotion.
Require Sponsored/Paid Partnership disclosure for cash or token compensation.
Keep payment records and public post URLs.
Do not give promoters discretionary posting authority over SATA-owned accounts.
items.publicDisclosure: Sponsored/Paid Partnership. Crypto assets involve risk. No price guarantee, no redemption promise, and liquidity can be thin and volatile.

items.title: Move BTC reserve custody toward multisig as the reserve grows
items.summary: Prepare a staged custody roadmap before the reserve grows materially toward the 1,000,000,000 sats target.
items.rationale: Single-signer custody is acceptable for early speed, but the project needs stronger controls as the reserve becomes material.
items.proposedAction: Draft a public multisig migration plan with signer roles, movement disclosure, verification steps, and fallback procedure.
riskReview: No agent may hold reserve signing keys.
No reserve movement should occur without a public note and chairman approval.
Reserve language must remain transparency-only, not a redemption promise or price floor.
items.publicDisclosure: The BTC reserve is a transparency metric only. It is not a redemption promise, guaranteed price floor, yield product, or market-support commitment.
